# Project Hyperion conical log-spiral head: isolated evaluation (generated by concepts/hyperion_report.py; MODELED)

Tested in isolation: no AXE2 rule or geometry constrains it; AXE2 appears only in the last comparison. Physics: concepts/clib.py (magpylib Biot-Savart, Neumann inductance, PI tail, eddy echo), self-check {'L_rel': 0.00033, 'M_rel': 0.0001, 'B_rel': 2e-05, 'ok': True}. Model script: concepts/hyperion_concept.py.

Assumptions: OPA211 1.1 nV/rtHz, 1 MHz, 1000-pulse average, SNR 5; no ground or EMI: absolute depths are optimistic, ratios are the result (threshold 0.174 uV); fast-switch case = 900 V-class SiC with a 460 V clamp and 60 pF node; litz 9.9 g/m; served-litz eps 2.2. Housing 300 x 18 mm, skid 2.0 mm, every coil above the same floor.

| 30 cm | 40.95 / 36.86 | 40.95 / 36.87 | 40.94 / 36.87 |
| 100 cm | 1.34 / 1.14 | 1.34 / 1.14 | 1.34 / 1.14 |

Where the gain comes from (vs its flat reference, %): {'1 cm': {'log_spacing_only_pct': 8.9, 'cone_only_pct': 2.3, 'both_pct': 11.8}, '30 cm': {'log_spacing_only_pct': -14.4, 'cone_only_pct': 4.1, 'both_pct': -9.9}}. On a common skid floor the cone vs the flat coil is {'1 cm': 7.1, '30 cm': -19.2, '100 cm': -18.2} %.

- the concept's own numbers re-run to the printed precision: the code is reproducible
- its evaluation point at '1 cm' (z = -10 mm) lies ABOVE the innermost turns (z = -12.3 mm): the +11.9 % is the inner turns being moved past the probe point
- its flat reference sits at the cone's outer (highest) edge; on a common skid floor the flat coil drops 12.3 mm and the cone loses at every depth
- its own log already shows the cone 10 % weaker at 30 cm and 15 % weaker at 100 cm: there is no focusing at depth

## 3. Three-phase 'spinning vortex'

- As written (interleaved spirals): {'max_angle_between_phase_fields_deg': {'[0, 0, -0.1]': 0.66, '[0, 0, -0.3]': 5.44, '[0.1, 0, -0.3]': 6.44, '[0, 0.1, -0.3]': 6.71}, 'note': 'three interleaved 120-deg-rotated spirals are three copies of the same axisymmetric source: the field directions agree to a fraction of a degree, so sequencing them spins nothing'}
- Sector coils (the build that does tilt the field): {'per_depth': {'100 mm': {'tilt_each_phase_deg': [52.9, 52.9, 52.9], 'edge_on_coin_coupling_vs_flat_coin_all_phases': 0.1945, 'single_phase_flat_coin_vs_all': 0.111}, '300 mm': {'tilt_each_phase_deg': [21.3, 21.3, 21.3], 'edge_on_coin_coupling_vs_flat_coin_all_phases': 0.017, 'single_phase_flat_coin_vs_all': 0.111}, '500 mm': {'tilt_each_phase_deg': [13.1, 13.1, 13.1], 'edge_on_coin_coupling_vs_flat_coin_all_phases': 0.0061, 'single_phase_flat_coin_vs_all': 0.111}}, 'note': "three 120-deg sector coils fired in turn DO tilt the field off the axis: an edge-on coin couples a few % of a flat one at shallow depth, falling with depth; each phase alone has about 1/9 of the full coil's squared field on axis"}
- the target stores the field present at each turn-off; a 25 kHz 'rotation' during the pulse is not seen by the target. Sequential phases are three separate measurements: 3 x the TX time per reading

## 5. Nanocrystalline sheets

{'transmission_below_static': 0.0741, 'field_loss_dB': 22.6, 'eddy_tau_us': 0.99, 'ferro_relax_tau_us': 13.3, 'closed_shell_shielding_dB': 24.9, 'mass_g_two_sheets': 50.2}

- a lower sheet sits between the coil and the ground: it shunts the field sideways (about the dB above at DC) and is itself a conducting, ferromagnetic disc inside the coil (eddy and ferromagnetic decay at the taus above)
- even a closed two-layer shell gives the closed-shell figure above at DC; a PI head must be open toward the ground, so >85 dB (17 800 x) from 10 Hz to 500 kHz is not reachable by any sheet that lets the TX out
- an upper sheet only is a known option (shields the electronics side) but it is a ferromagnetic target inside the coil: place it far above the winding or omit it

## 6. Metatron's Cube RX

{'nodes': 13, 'layout': "Metatron's Cube: centre, 6 at 54 mm, 6 at 108 mm; node radius 26 mm", 'turns_per_node': 36, 'trace': '0.25 / 0.25 mm, 2 oz (70 um)', 'R_node_ohm': 3.83, 'johnson_nV': 0.25, 'L_node_uH': 78.9, 'M_tx_node_uH': [5.705, 6.938, 6.889, 6.948, 6.999, 7.021, 7.021, 0.427, 0.343, 0.383, 0.43, 0.476, 0.513], 'V_node_at_turnoff_V': [30.0, 36.5, 2.2], 'pair_residual_uH': 0.0615, 'residual_per_0p1mm_misplacement_uH': 0.0126, 'V_pair_residual_per_0p1mm_V': 0.07, 'target_coupling': {'100 mm': {'single_node_vs_mono': 0.1414, 'best_pair_diff_vs_mono': 0.14949}, '300 mm': {'single_node_vs_mono': 0.081, 'best_pair_diff_vs_mono': 0.02262}, '500 mm': {'single_node_vs_mono': 0.0716, 'best_pair_diff_vs_mono': 0.00965}}, 'ground_pair_rejection_level': 0.02022, 'ground_pair_rejection_tilt3deg': 0.22}

- planar coils on a flat flex sense only the field normal to the board; '45 / 90 degree vector planes' need folded or vertical coils (an 18 mm stack limits a vertical node to about 14 mm x 50 mm)
- single nodes inside the TX see the full primary: tens to hundreds of volts at turn-off; they are not in a null
- opposite node pairs cancel the TX and a level, uniform ground by symmetry (a gradiometer); the same symmetry cancels a centred target, and a 3 deg tilt breaks the ground balance
- a 26 mm node collects a few % of the mono coil's target flux; differential pairs collect less at depth (gradient falls one power of z faster)

## 7. Named parts

- **IXTY02N100D**: UNVERIFIED: no datasheet found for this part number; the IXTY01N100D family sheet (IXYS 2006) gives 1000 V, ID 100 mA, RDS(on) 90-110 ohm at VGS 0; distributors list 400 mA (Tc) / 80 ohm. a depletion-mode small-signal FET conducts ~0.1-0.4 A class current with ~80-110 ohm on-resistance: it cannot carry a 10 A coil pulse (10 A x 80 ohm = 800 V drop). Normally-on: with no gate bias at power-up it shorts the coil across the supply. Used in PI as a current source or start-up device, not as the TX switch
- **BAV199**: NXP/Philips BAV199 datasheet: VR 75 V, VRRM 85 V, IF 160 mA, leakage typ 3 pA, trr 0.8 typ / 3 us max (10 mA / 10 mA), Cd 2 pF. a good low-leakage preamp clamp, but slow: its 0.8-3 us recovery after the flyback alone exceeds the claimed 0.8 us settle. It is not a Schottky and not fast-recovery
- **OPA211**: TI SBOS377L: 1.1 nV/rtHz at 1 kHz, GBW 80 MHz (G 100) / 45 MHz (G 1), 27 V/us, +-2.25 to +-18 V, settling 700 ns to 16 bit. a sound PI preamp choice; its settling (0.7 us) and overload recovery also sit at or above the claimed 0.8 us
- **LITZ_1050_48**: MWS LITZ-1050-48-T2 sheet not obtained (UNVERIFIED part number); copper area from strand count: 1050 x 48 AWG = 0.818 mm2, 0.0217 ohm/m. text says silicone-insulated in one place and PU-nylon served in another; 22 m on the BOM vs about 11 m per 20-turn spiral
- **FERRITE_9478012002**: not a Fair-Rite catalogue number (-MOD); 78 material data from fair-rite.com: mu_i 2300, Bsat 4800 G at 5 Oe, rho 200 ohm cm, Tc > 200 C. see ferrite block
- **NC_0050_S**: not found in Magnetics Inc literature: UNVERIFIED; modelled as FINEMET-class (mu_r 50 000, rho 1.2 uohm m, 7.3 g/cm3, ASSUMED). see shields block

## What survives

- sector / multi-coil TX fired in sequence: a real way to tilt the excitation and see edge-on targets (costs TX time and field per phase)
- differential planar RX pairs (gradiometer) for TX and level-ground cancellation: real, and the same principle as AXE2's quadrupole RX boards
- OPA211 preamp and a slotted / finger Faraday shield: sound, standard
- low-leakage BAV199 clamps: fine for leakage, too slow for a sub-microsecond gate
